experiment: STT time-to-final tail: bounded finalize budget (1.2 s) with partial-snapshot fallback
method: Warm 15-call WebRTC sample (5 billing clips x 3 reps) via scripts/webrtc_live_client.py against the real stack: Gradium streaming STT/TTS + Mistral RAG backend (top-k=5, WEB-036), co-located dev host, WAV clips padded with a low-amplitude noise tail (Opus DTX). 1 warm-up call discarded, telemetry reset, then 15 measured turns. Per-slice scored by scripts/streaming_latency_report.py; clean per-call weighting (WebRTC fresh session per offer, n=15).

finalize_fallback.note: The single stalled-terminal turn was finalized from the partials already received (non-empty snapshot) and answered. The other 14 finalized naturally on the provider terminal (<= 1095 ms). All 15 turns produced stt.transcript.final (0 unavailable), so the cap cost no turn to word-starvation.

comparison_p95_ms.note: Combined levers (top-k=5 WEB-036 + finalize budget WEB-035) vs the WEB-032 baseline and the WEB-036 STT-lever-less rescore.

outcome.lever_effect: The finalize budget capped the STT time-to-final tail at ~1.2 s (was up to ~4 s), removing the pathological outliers while all normal turns finalized on the real terminal. Combined with top-k=5, mouth-to-ear p95 dropped 3743 -> 2777 ms (-26%) and time_to_first_audio p95 3393 -> 2427 ms (-28%) vs the WEB-032 baseline.
outcome.gate: ADR-0029 still FAIL (m2e p95 2777 > 1500; TTFA p95 2427 > 1200), but the STT tail is no longer the dominant blocker.
remaining_levers: backend first-token (Lever B, LLM-provider benchmark): p95 ~1199 ms, LLM-first-token dominated and model-inherent — the largest remaining post-EOT slice.

finalize budget could be lowered further (e.g. ~900 ms) but must be WER-validated: at 1.2 s the fallback only fires on genuinely stalled terminals (partials long complete); tightening risks capping turns whose partials are still arriving.
end-of-turn hold (350 ms) trimming carries a false-cut risk (TASK-WEB-015 floor 250 ms).
outcome.wer_note: Transcripts are redacted in telemetry (PII), so a formal normalized-WER pass is not derivable from this dump. Proxy evidence: 15/15 stt.transcript.final, 0 unavailable, all turns answered audibly; the 1 fallback turn returned a non-empty partial snapshot (same join as the terminal path) and was answered. A dedicated WER pass with reference transcripts remains the QA-GO closer.
